NOTE (Wed 22 Jul) — BBC live blog (Reuters-bylined summary): "VAT on electricity: ... The government expects the cost to be £850m, which it will finance through reallocation of funds from the cancellation of the Digital ID programme. It has insisted the change is 'fully funded'." I.e. Burnham is SCRAPPING Sir Keir Starmer's flagship Digital ID (BritCard) scheme to pay for the six-month cut of VAT (5%->0) on household electricity bills from October (saves ~£45/household). Independent live blog: PM's spokesperson said the electricity measure "is fuly [sic] funded... funded for this financial year and the cost of this action for this financial year is being funded through the cancellation of the digital ID programme." Distinct from the £2 bus-fare cap, which is funded separately (£454m reallocated from DESNZ / international climate-finance-to-loans switch). Do NOT conflate the two funding sources.
